slices.title: Typed triple identity and canonical signed records
slices.goal: Define general typed-byte triple terms, object references, LogicalGraphId, source_record provenance and exact ContentId/PayloadId/EnvelopeId preimages. Own only term.rs, record.rs and their test; do not create or edit graph/mod.rs or crate-root exports.
slices.enables: Graph and attribute surfaces share typed bytes and non-self-referential signed identities; adapters can add indexes without changing signed truth.

requires.description: Creates the common graph/mod.rs skeleton and shared profile/vector interfaces, without exporting absent leaf modules. This slice uses direct-path leaf imports in its integration test. Final public module/export wiring is owned by 9110-09 after this slice completes.
Consume the additive identity-profile/legacy compatibility contract; do not edit or re-sign legacy artifact bytes.

after.description: Consume any later Atlas ContentId mapping only in an Atlas-specific adapter; the typed-byte graph core does not own or block on the producer investigation.

oracle.expected: Reference encoder and independent verifier agree on exact canonical Body, raw PayloadId, profile-byte ContentId, complete signed-envelope EnvelopeId, source_record provenance, and arbitrary typed-byte round trips; self-referential IDs and ambiguous encodings reject.
oracle.verifier: graph_term_codec.rs imports ../src/graph/term.rs and ../src/graph/record.rs with explicit #[path] modules until 9110-09 performs public wiring. Independent reference codec and known-answer vectors compare exact outputs; no vector hashes an ID into its own preimage.

slices.rollback: Remove only the new graph module and test files; keep crosscut-owned crate-root exports/profile vectors and all existing signed bytes unchanged.

slices.title: Rebuildable ordered triple indexes and streaming scans
slices.goal: Add an initial redb materialization with rebuildable SPO/POS/OSP indexes and bounded continuation scans; index bytes remain derived and outside signed authority.
slices.enables: Bounded graph patterns and pages execute without loading the entire LogicalGraphId.

requires.description: Typed terms, AssertionId and graph record boundary.
Measured candidate-engine bake-off and selected V2 backend/profile recommendation.
Common id-store crate-root export/port registration; graph index remains a separate module.

oracle.expected: Index rebuild and all supported leading-component scans return exactly the same assertion IDs as the pure typed-set matcher at a fixed frontier, including shuffled ingestion, missing-index and corruption cases.
oracle.verifier: Independent in-memory typed-set matcher and rebuild-from-signed-evidence pass.

slices.rollback: Drop only the new graph index module and tests; signed record bytes remain authoritative and can be rescanned without an index.

slices.title: Benchmark real graph encoding and storage candidates
slices.goal: Measure actual candidate engines on one shared typed-byte corpus: deterministic chunked binary, current redb tuple-key materialization, SQLite JSONB, and normalized SQLite BLOB rows; report storage, indexed query, streaming/page and write costs without choosing from the toy serialization result.
slices.enables: A measured V2 storage recommendation with raw artifacts, engine/version/config metadata, repeatable fixture and explicit limits.

requires.description: Canonical typed-byte terms and shared deterministic corpus/reference oracle.

research_evidence: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8949 — CBOR typed bytes, canonical/profile considerations and streaming items (retrieved 2026-11-12).
https://www.sqlite.org/json1.html — SQLite JSONB is engine-private; documented JSONB size/operation properties (retrieved 2026-11-12).
pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/tuple.rs — current typed ordered tuple-key codec.
pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/tag_index.rs — current prefix/range indexes and index-order alternatives.
doc/2026-11-13T03-40-00Z_design_id-atlas-summit/part-a-graph/graph-encoding-toy.py and experiment-output.txt — deterministic serialization-only toy, explicitly not candidate-engine evidence.

oracle.expected: Runner executes the candidate-engine harness, then emits and validates raw results covering every engine/workload cell, engine/schema/index versions, byte/type round-trip oracle, repeated runs, query/page/write/storage measures and limits; missing, inconsistent or unrepeatable cells fail. No universal winner is asserted.
oracle.verifier: Strictly parsed runner invokes the exact redb/SQLite candidate harness before validation; independent artifact validator recomputes fixture hashes, checks matrix completeness/report consistency, and compares query outputs to the reference model.

slices.rollback: Remove only the benchmark test, report, results and validator; no production codec/schema/index is modified by this research slice.
slices.trigger: Run before freezing the V2 candidate storage/encoding choice; do not treat the existing stdlib toy as this candidate-engine benchmark.

slices.title: Bounded read-only triple-pattern API and cursors
slices.goal: Expose conjunctive patterns over TermPattern and LogicalGraphId with stable ordering, opaque snapshot cursor, mandatory page limit, server-side authorization and an operator-validated resource profile.
slices.enables: Attributes, social projections and optional visualization share one authorized graph-read path and source_record provenance.

requires.description: Typed terms, LogicalGraphId and source_record provenance.
Common crate-root export and interface registration; no graph ownership of lib.rs.

after.description: Prefer the measured index adapter when available; API contract remains backend-independent.

oracle.expected: Reference matcher and paged query agree at a fixed frontier; cursor pages concatenate without omission/duplication, and unauthorized or over-budget queries never report complete.
oracle.verifier: Independent pure matcher over canonical typed-triple fixtures and cursor-page concatenation checker.

slices.rollback: Remove only graph query/cursor modules and test; no event bytes or existing query-local/remote API is rewritten.

slices.title: Bounded graph viewer over query pages
slices.goal: Build an optional native-shell graph viewer over the same authorized paged query API, marking cycles, provenance, missing references and truncation.
slices.enables: Humans can inspect graph neighborhoods without a second graph store or false-complete whole-graph picture.

requires.description: Authorized QueryPage and provenance contract.

oracle.expected: Golden cyclic/over-budget fixture visibly includes a back-reference, provenance, missing-reference state and truncation; rendered node/edge set equals authorized QueryPage rows.
oracle.verifier: Independent golden graph fixture and exact row-set comparison.

slices.rollback: Remove the optional viewer command/test; the query API and graph data model remain usable without UI.
slices.trigger: Only when a human-facing graph inspection surface is prioritized; not required for V2 query conformance.

slices.title: Evaluate query-language options without selecting one by default
slices.goal: Compare typed patterns, SPARQL subset, SQL/PGQ, and traversal/API alternatives against concrete interoperability and safety needs; recommendation may adopt none and no parser is implied.
slices.enables: Any later syntax remains an adapter over the typed API with explicitly bounded semantics, or the project records that no named language is justified.

requires.description: Typed API semantics form the comparison baseline.

research_evidence: https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/ — SPARQL 1.1 feature and graph-pattern semantics (retrieved 2026-11-12).
https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/ — RDF term and graph model; triples alone do not imply RDF (retrieved 2026-11-12).
doc/2026-11-08_decision_id5909_sql_pgq_capability.md — typed pattern IR, PGQ options and backend limits.
doc/2026-11-08_design_id5837.md and doc/2026-11-08T08-10-00Z_design_id5782_graphical_client_tooling.md — bounded graph reads and truthful visualization limits.

oracle.expected: Decision report compares each named option on concrete semantics, RDF need, portability, limits and risks; the matrix permits `none` as the result and contains no unrequested parser/API selection.
oracle.verifier: Independent validator compares the report claims to machine-readable option matrix and cited source inventory; unsupported feature claims fail.

slices.rollback: Remove only the option matrix, decision report and validator; no parser or runtime query API is implemented by this research slice.
slices.trigger: Only if an external RDF/interoperability consumer or a product requirement makes language selection actionable; the default outcome may be no named language.

slices.title: Signed user-attribute definitions and policy
slices.goal: Define signed attribute objects, target scope and explicit closed/open/moderated policy, distinct from Atlas and content-location metadata.
slices.enables: Append admission can apply a verified attribute policy before publishing accepted values.

requires.description: Typed terms, LogicalGraphId and signed object identities.
Tenant-scope authorization interface for attribute definition and resolution; consume its owned boundary only.

oracle.expected: Canonical attribute definitions round-trip; malformed scope, unauthorized policy edits and cross-tenant references reject under the independent schema and tenancy model.
oracle.verifier: Reference attribute schema validator plus #9083 tenant-authority interface fixture.

slices.rollback: Remove only new attribute schema/module/test; no Atlas metadata or content-location records are rewritten.

slices.title: Append submission, mandatory pending gate and atomic approval
slices.goal: Verify signatures before pending/admission; force every non-group submitter to Pending even when open; directly accept only eligible in-group submitters; approve by CAS after membership, policy and revocation recheck.
slices.enables: The accepted list is published only after its signed-evidence and moderation gate, with immutable authoritative order.

requires.description: Signed attribute and open/closed/moderated policy.
Current tenant/membership authorization interface used by admission CAS; no policy is copied into graph code.

oracle.expected: Invalid signatures never enter pending/accepted; non-group submission remains pending on open attributes; approval CAS rechecks current membership/policy/revocation; same idempotency key with different bytes conflicts; order never rewrites or wraps.
oracle.verifier: Independent model-based state machine with concurrent policy changes, duplicate submissions, restart/replay and epoch/sequence exhaustion.

slices.rollback: Disable only the new append protocol adapter; retain validated signed submission evidence and never project Pending as accepted during rollback.

slices.title: Nested topic/comment objects and bounded feed projections
slices.goal: Define immutable topic/comment/reaction/feed references and iterative bounded traversal without prescribing a specific app's ranking.
slices.enables: Feeds, profiles and bulletin-board projections compose over signed graph objects.

requires.description: Typed terms, logical graph IDs and signed provenance.
Attribute object/policy vocabulary.
Append acceptance projection and authoritative sequence.

oracle.expected: Iterative traversal of nested and cyclic fixtures obeys the selected deployment profile and returns exact authorized relations with explicit back-reference/truncation state.
oracle.verifier: Independent reference traversal model over the signed relation set and resource profile.

slices.rollback: Remove the social projection adapter without deleting underlying signed graph objects or accepted append records.

slices.title: Scoped social-feed freshness cursor and delta pages
slices.goal: Allocate a durable projection-ledger sequence for each complete `(tenant, query, generation)` feed entry, while retaining each source authority/epoch/sequence and pinned frontier; cursor `last_projection_seq` drives latest/since/before pages.
slices.enables: Clients check latest/since/before without a full forum rescan and expired cursors never claim no changes.

requires.description: Accepted server epoch/sequence log.
Feed projection and query scope.

oracle.expected: Two source authorities with identical source epoch/sequence yield distinct, ordered projection entries; latest/since/before use stable projection sequence plus entry ID at a pinned frontier; access/moderation generation changes invalidate; reset, retention gap, bad MAC and query/tenant replay return typed expired/mismatch states.
oracle.verifier: Independent complete-feed projection-ledger model interleaving two source authorities, restart, deletion/moderation, generation changes and retention gaps.

slices.rollback: Invalidate the new cursor generation and require a full scoped refresh; do not change accepted event ordering or claim global replica freshness.

slices.title: Canonical v1-succeeds-v2 version DAG and branch projection
slices.goal: Store `(predecessor_v1, succeeds, successor_v2)`, validate same logical object and acyclic lineage, adapt equivalent Supersede records explicitly, and preserve competing heads.
slices.enables: Immutable edits and branch-aware current-version views without silent last-writer-wins.

requires.description: Assertion identity and source_record provenance.

oracle.expected: Stored relation direction is v1→v2; complete cycles reject, incomplete ancestry remains pending, and every valid concurrent head remains observable.
oracle.verifier: Independent version-DAG model and explicit legacy Supersede mapping fixtures.

slices.rollback: Disable new version projection while preserving signed v1/v2 objects and their original edge/evidence bytes.

slices.title: Default ancestor-comment carry with origin marker
slices.goal: In the V3 social projection, carry eligible ancestor comments into the default descendant view with an old-version marker and transitive origin while retaining the original target and branch identity.
slices.enables: Social readers see historical discussion on v2 without implying comments were authored against revised content; V2 only stores/version-checks succeeds edges.

requires.description: Version DAG and selected branch ancestry.
Comment object identities and relation model.

oracle.expected: Each eligible ancestor comment appears once with immutable original target/origin and old-version marker; access/moderation/deletion filters still apply and sibling branches do not leak.
oracle.verifier: Independent version-DAG comment projection model keyed by immutable comment ID.

slices.rollback: Disable carried-comment view projection; retain comments on their original versions and leave all signed targets unchanged.

slices.title: Deletion requests, moderation queue and local true-delete states
slices.goal: Represent author/group deletion request, moderation queue, projection hide and server-policy true-delete as distinct signed states and bounded batch transitions.
slices.enables: A server moderates locally without rewriting signed identity or claiming global erasure.

requires.description: Signed assertion and source evidence identities.
Owner/group attribute authority boundaries.

oracle.expected: Request/queue/hide/physical-delete remain distinct; batch retries are idempotent, retained evidence follows policy, and local actions do not mutate another replica's signed set.
oracle.verifier: Independent deletion-state model with retention and two-replica fixtures.

slices.rollback: Disable the new local moderation/deletion projection; keep signed requests and evidence intact and restore prior serving policy only where allowed.

slices.title: Fenced reference-aware graph garbage collection
slices.goal: Fence references with a deletion-generation tombstone and CAS against reference-index generation/retention; consume #9137 and #9084 semantics before physical shared-object removal.
slices.enables: GC cannot race a fresh reference or let an older worker delete after a newer retain/reference generation.

requires.description: Distinct deletion/retention state machine.
Rebuildable reference-index generation and storage transaction boundary.
GC retention/large-object collection policy and fencing interface.
Reference-vs-copy semantics and authority boundary for shared objects.

oracle.expected: Interleaved reference creation, stale GC worker, restart and policy retention never remove referenced/retained bytes; an old fence cannot delete after generation advance.
oracle.verifier: Independent concurrent reference/GC state model with CAS/fence generation oracle.

slices.rollback: Keep physical GC disabled and preserve all existing objects; remove only the new planner/executor and fencing index.
slices.trigger: Do not enable shared-object physical deletion until #9137 and #9084 contracts are available and the adapter has fenced atomic compare-and-delete.

slices.title: Immutable signer-bound space address and local petnames
slices.goal: Verify the canonical typed `[null, public-key-bytes]` binding offline; keep its address immutable and petnames local; successor control uses a verified chain there or an explicit signed redirect to a new address.
slices.enables: Clients attribute a space binding to a signer without trusting its server or silently replacing the original key at the same coordinates.

requires.description: Typed byte terms, ObjectRef and canonical signed-record verification.

oracle.expected: Independent offline verifier accepts exact canonical binding and rejects wrong signer/position/version; transfer cannot mutate original address; new-address redirect needs old-key proof; petname changes neither ID nor authorization.
oracle.verifier: Independent signature verifier and canonical address decoder; existing petname locality contract is regression-tested.

slices.rollback: Remove new binding module and tests; preserve existing petname storage and all canonical addresses already issued.

slices.title: Bounded delegation chains and two-key control transfer
slices.goal: Implement scoped attenuation and distinct accepted transfer with replay protection, signed expiry, cycle rejection, finite chain budget and latest-frontier revocation freshness.
slices.enables: A location write can be delegated without conflating a continuing grant with replacement ownership.

requires.description: Immutable signer-bound address and successor presentation.
Canonical signed identities and typed array-address terms.

oracle.expected: No grant exceeds parent scope; nonce replay, cycles, expiry, stale frontier and over-depth chains fail closed; transfer requires both keys over identical transfer/scope/challenge/domain/expiry bytes.
oracle.verifier: Independent authority-chain model with nonce uniqueness and signed-time/frontier rules.

slices.rollback: Disable delegation/transfer authorization and require original controller authorization; preserve all signed grant/transfer evidence.

slices.title: Mutual cross-signed key-link challenge
slices.goal: Represent mutual key-link claims over the same challenge bytes binding ordered pair, purpose/domain, scope, nonce and expiry; do not merge identity, account or authority from link status alone.
slices.enables: Clients can display a verified mutual key claim without silently merging accounts or privileges.

requires.description: Signer-bound key identities and local trust display.

oracle.expected: Only both valid signatures over identical challenge bytes become mutual; unilateral, unrelated, mismatched-scope/nonce/domain/expiry or revoked claims stay pending/invalid and never merge account or authorization state.
oracle.verifier: Independent signature verification and exact challenge-field equality checker.

slices.rollback: Disable mutual-link projection; retain signed statements and keep both keys independently addressable.
